Maya Patel: Heads up — saw a 3x p99 jump for model/llama-13b on pool-gpu-3 between 14:12–14:25 UTC. Traces point to a kernel auto-switch: `kernel_select: kernel=fp32_fallback reason=kv_quant_mismatch`
Sam Liu: Ugh. Did batching change? Any big batches around the switch?
Maya Patel: Yeah, batch size histogram spiked — most workers jumped from median 1->40+ in ~8s. The batching heuristic extended the accumulation window after seeing a sustained steady qps from tenant analytics-pro.
Jin Park: Can you paste the runtime log lines around 14:13? Also, what was the KV cache miss/evict rate?
Maya Patel: Log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:13:02Z runtime: batch_window_ms=120 -> 600 (heuristic)
2026-03-15T14:13:03Z kernel_select: chosen=fp32_fallback reason=kv_quant_mismatch
2026-03-15T14:13:03Z kvcache: miss=0.78 evict=712
```
Anika Rao: I sampled KV keys for that tenant — extremely high cardinality of prefixes (many short-lived keys). TTLs are low but churn rate is enormous; eviction churn was eating the cache so model couldn't get fast KV hits -> fallback path.
autoscaler-bot: [autoscaler] pool-gpu-3 scaled +2 gpus at 2026-03-15T14:14:00Z due to queue/backlog
Ryan O'Connor: Repro command to saturate approx same pattern: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --script ./scripts/seq_prefix_load.lua http://pool-gpu-3/v1/generate` — the lua script sends many distinct prefixes which triggers large KV growth.
Sam Liu: Short-term mitigations we can try: 1) cap per-tenant batch_tokens (e.g., 2048), 2) tighten batch window (20ms) for best-effort tenancy, 3) enforce per-tenant KV memory quota to avoid cross-tenant thrash.
Maya Patel: I pushed a hotfix: set `batch_window_ms=20` and `max_batch_tokens=2048` on pool-gpu-3 for best-effort tenants (+ applied tenant-level admission). Observed p99 fall back to ~1.1x baseline within 60s. :relieved:
Jin Park: Nice. For kernel side, we should avoid silent fp32 fallback when quant metadata is ambiguous. Maybe add a soft-fail that logs and keeps int8_strict for shared pools, rather than switching to fp32 and blowing memory.
Anika Rao: Long-term: add per-tenant KV quotas + eviction-preference (prefer evicting cold keys of offending tenant), plus a sampling profiler for KV churn. I already started an experiment that tags keys with tenant-id heat.
Ryan O'Connor: Also file an incident -> INC-7891 with timeline and remediation steps. Recommend assigning follow-ups: perf/eng-runtime to add admission control, infra to add quota metrics, and runtime to add kernel pinning flag.
Sam Liu: Agreed. I'll own the follow-up ticket for batching heuristics and add a unit test for window growth.
Maya Patel: TL;DR: noisy tenant with many distinct prefixes caused KV evictions -> high KV miss -> kernel auto-switch to fp32 fallback under memory/quant mismatch + expanded batch sizes amplified latency. Hotfix applied (batch window cap + batch token cap) restored latency. Next: per-tenant KV quotas, kernel-policy safeguards, admission control.
Ryan O'Connor: Good postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: Adding logs and a perf flamegraph to INC-7891. Link: /incidents/INC-7891/perf-graphs (uploaded).
Jin Park: For follow-ups, let's also add an integration test that simulates high-prefix-cardinality traffic to shared pools to catch regressions early.
Anika Rao: I'll export KV miss-rate dashboards and add alerts when evict_rate > 300/min for any pool.
Sam Liu: Cool. Closing the thread after we confirm the metric thresholds and ticket ownerships.
Maya Patel: Thanks all — marking this as monitored for the next 24h.
